ing: or thin white fish such as tilapia
st: Rub the fish with the juice of 1 lime and [[0.5 tsp]] of the salt. Let it sit for [[15 minutes]], then rinse and pat dry.
Melt [[1 tbsp]] butter in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4 minutes, then add the tomato, thyme, whole pepper, and black pepper. Cook 5 minutes.
Add [[0.5 cup]] of the water and the fish, folding the fillets into the sauce. Cover and steam gently for 8 minutes until the fish flakes. Squeeze in the second lime.
For the cou-cou, bring [[3 cups]] water and the okra to a boil with [[1 tsp]] salt. Simmer 10 minutes until tender.
Mix the cornmeal with [[0.5 cup]] cold water to a smooth paste in a bowl.
Lower the heat. Strain out a little okra water if too much. Slowly pour the cornmeal paste into the okra pot, stirring hard with a wooden spoon.
Cook on low for 8 to 10 minutes, beating and folding, until the cou-cou is thick, smooth, and pulls from the pot side. Stir in [[1 tbsp]] butter.
Mold the cou-cou in a buttered bowl, turn out onto a plate, and top with the remaining butter. Serve the fish and sauce beside it.
Soak the salt cod in cold water overnight, changing the water 3 times. Simmer in fresh water for 15 minutes, drain, and cool.
Flake the fish with a fork, removing any bones and skin.
Mix the flour and baking powder in a bowl.
Add the flaked fish, onion, bell pepper, thyme, Scotch bonnet, green onions, and black pepper.
Stir in the cold water to form a thick, scoopable batter. Rest it for [[15 minutes]].
Heat the oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Drop tablespoons of batter into the oil in batches. Fry 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until deep golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with pepper sauce.
Simmer the pork in salted water for 1 hour 15 minutes until very tender. Drain and cool.
Cut the pork into bite-size pieces and place in a bowl.
Add the cucumber, onion, Scotch bonnet, lime juice, vinegar, and [[1 tsp]] salt. Toss well and chill overnight for best flavor, or at least [[2 hours]].
For the pudding, heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease a loaf pan with the butter.
Mix the grated sweet potatoes with the sugar, thyme, black pepper, and [[1 tsp]] salt. Add a splash of water if dry.
Pack the mixture tightly into the pan and cover with foil.
Bake for 1 hour 15 minutes until the pudding is firm. Cool 10 minutes, then slice.
Serve a slice of warm pudding with a scoop of cold souse beside it.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Grease a 9 by 13 inch baking dish.
Boil the macaroni in well-salted water for 8 minutes until almost tender. Drain well.
Return the hot macaroni to the pot and stir in the butter until melted.
Add the onion, mustard, ketchup, salt, and pepper.
Stir in [[2 cups]] of the cheese and let it start to melt.
Whisk the eggs and milk together, then stir into the macaroni.
Pour into the baking dish and top with the remaining [[1 cup]] cheese.
Bake for 35 minutes until set and golden brown on top. Rest for [[10 minutes]] before cutting.

ing: such as flying fish, tilapia, or mahi-mahi
st: Cut the fish into portions that fit your rolls. Season with the salt, pepper, and lime juice and let it sit for [[10 minutes]].
Set up the flour, beaten egg, and breadcrumbs in three shallow dishes.
Coat each piece of fish in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering, about 350°F (175°C).
Fry the fish for 3 minutes per side until golden and cooked through to 145°F (63°C).
Drain on paper towels.
Split the rolls and layer in lettuce and tomato slices.
Add the hot fish and spoon on the pepper sauce. Close and eat while warm.
Wear gloves when handling the Scotch bonnets and do not touch your eyes. Remove the stems.
Put the peppers, onion, garlic, and vinegar in a pot.
Simmer over low heat for 15 minutes until the peppers are very soft.
Let the mixture cool for [[10 minutes]], then pour it into a blender.
Add the mustard, turmeric, salt, sugar, and lime juice.
Blend until completely smooth. Add a splash of water if too thick.
Pour into a clean bottle or jar and chill for [[1 day]] for the flavor to develop.
Keep refrigerated for up to 1 month. Use a few drops at a time.

ing: or foil squares, cut into 8-inch pieces
st: If using banana leaves, pass them over a flame for a few seconds to make them soft, then wipe clean.
Mix the cornmeal, flour, sugar, nutmeg, cinnamon, and salt in a large bowl.
Stir in the grated pumpkin and sweet potato, the coconut, and raisins.
Add the melted butter and coconut milk and mix to a thick, wet batter. It should drop slowly from a spoon.
Spoon about 1/3 cup of the batter into the middle of each leaf.
Fold the leaf over the batter, tuck in the ends, and tie with string, forming a flat packet.
Place the packets on a steamer rack over simmering water. Cover and steam for 1 hour 15 minutes, adding water as needed.
Cool for 10 minutes. Open the parcels and eat warm.

ing: or use pineapple juice for a non-alcoholic drink
st: To make the syrup, stir equal parts sugar and hot water until dissolved. Cool completely.
Fill a large pitcher half way with ice.
Pour in the rum, lime juice, and [[6 fl oz]] of the syrup.
Add the cold water and the bitters. Stir for 20 seconds until the pitcher feels cold.
Taste it and add more syrup or lime until the sweet and sour are balanced.
Strain into four glasses filled with fresh ice.
Grate nutmeg over the top and add a lime wheel to each glass.
